new_page.description: Delta MLS® benchmark prices for September 2026: $1,113,100 for a typical Tsawwassen home, down 4.3% in a year, with detached, townhouse and apartment trends.
new_page.h1: Delta Real Estate Market Stats, September 2026

faq_heading: Delta market stats: your questions answered

blocks.text: The boards report Delta in 3 parts: Tsawwassen, Ladner and North Delta. In September 2026, Tsawwassen had the highest all-home benchmark at $1,113,100 and North Delta the lowest at $1,011,500, a gap of $101,600. Over twelve months the three-part spread runs Tsawwassen down 4.3%, Ladner down 6.9%, North Delta down 9.1%.
Tsawwassen at a glance, September 2026
Tsawwassen had an all-home benchmark of $1,113,100 (down 4.3% over the year), with detached at $1,508,500, townhouses at $886,000 and apartments at $556,000.
Tsawwassen market stats in full
Ladner at a glance, September 2026
Ladner had an all-home benchmark of $1,033,700 (down 6.9% over the year), with detached at $1,284,100, townhouses at $919,800 and apartments at $586,400.
Ladner market stats in full
North Delta benchmark prices and trends, September 2026

A typical North Delta home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $1,011,500 in September 2026. That is down 1.8% on the month, down 5.0% over three months, down 6.4% over six months and down 9.1% over the year. Over three years it is down 17.2%, and over five years down 10.9%.
The weakest one-year move in North Delta was for an apartment homes at −11.6%; the strongest was a townhouse at −4.7%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,159,600) and an apartment ($479,000) is $680,600, and a townhouse ($845,600) sits $366,600 above the apartment benchmark.
Against the Fraser Valley Board area, where the all-home benchmark was $861,300, North Delta is 17.4% above. Over the year the Fraser Valley Board area moved down 7.2% against down 9.1% here.
Of the 8 areas this board reports, North Delta ranks 1 by all-home benchmark, with South Surrey & White Rock below it at $990,300.

Detached homes in North Delta: benchmark $1,159,600, down 2.3% in a month, down 5.9% in three months, down 7.4% in six months, down 11.0% in a year, down 17.1% in three years and down 11.1% in five. That is 10.8% below the detached benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($1,300,000).

Townhouse homes in North Delta: benchmark $845,600, little changed at −0.6% in a month, down 2.7% in three months, down 5.3% in six months, down 4.7% in a year, down 12.9% in three years and up 2.1% in five. That is 13.5% above the townhouse benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($745,300).

Apartment homes in North Delta: benchmark $479,000, little changed at −1.3% in a month, down 5.2% in three months, down 5.4% in six months, down 11.6% in a year, down 17.4% in three years and little changed at +1.3% in five. That is 3.7% above the apartment benchmark for the Fraser Valley Board area ($461,800).

blocks.text: What the Delta figure is
The $1,113,100 Tsawwassen figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for September 2026.

faq.q: What is the benchmark price of a home in Delta?
faq.a: In September 2026, a typical Tsawwassen home was $1,113,100, with detached at $1,508,500. In September 2026, a typical Ladner home was $1,033,700, with detached at $1,284,100. In September 2026, a typical North Delta home was $1,011,500, with detached at $1,159,600.

faq.q: Are Delta home prices rising or falling?
faq.a: Tsawwassen is down 4.3% over twelve months and down 3.1% over three months. Ladner is down 6.9% over twelve months and down 5.3% over three months. North Delta is down 9.1% over twelve months and down 5.0% over three months.
